title_en: John Waldron on GDP Growth, AI, and the M&A Outlook
title_zh: John Waldron 谈 GDP 增长、AI 与并购（M&A）前景
subtitle_zh: 高盛总裁兼COO John Waldron 谈增长韧性、AI 落地与并购回暖。
description: John Waldron on GDP Growth, AI, and the M&A Outlook

turns.en: Music Markets are navigating an unusual mix of resilient growth, shifting rate expectations, and rapid technological change. Against that backdrop, how is Goldman Sachs reading the moment and positioning the firm for what comes next? I'm Allison Nathan and this is Goldman Sachs exchanges. Music
turns.zh: （音乐）如今的市场正处在一种不同寻常的组合之中：增长仍有韧性、利率预期不断转变、技术变革飞速推进。在这样的背景下，Goldman Sachs 如何解读当下，又如何为公司布局下一步？我是 Allison Nathan，欢迎收听 Goldman Sachs Exchanges。（音乐）

turns.en: Today I'm joined by John Waldron, President and Chief Operating Officer of Goldman Sachs. We'll discuss the current sentiment among business leaders and investors. The outlook for markets and the economy, and where Goldman Sachs sees its next avenues for growth. John, welcome back to exchanges. Thank you, Allison. Good to be here.
turns.zh: 今天做客节目的是 Goldman Sachs 总裁兼首席运营官（President and Chief Operating Officer）John Waldron。我们会聊聊企业领袖和投资人当下的心态、市场与经济的走向，以及 Goldman Sachs 认为下一阶段的增长点在哪里。John，欢迎再次来到 Exchanges。——谢谢你，Allison，很高兴再来。

turns.en: John, let's just start with a quick gut check. There's so much going on in the world, and markets, as you will know, have been increasingly volatile. You spend much of your time with our corporate and investing clients. How would you describe the mood among business leaders and investors today, compared to say a year ago?
turns.zh: John，我们先来个快速的直觉判断。世界上正在发生的事情太多了，而且你也清楚，市场的波动越来越大。你很多时间都花在服务企业客户和投资人客户上。跟比如说一年前相比，你会怎么形容现在企业领袖和投资人的情绪？

turns.en: I think still, generally speaking, optimistic. Maybe a little more cautious at the margin, versus where it would have been six, twelve months ago. Inflation is higher, and that feeds through a lot of businesses. So particularly for CEOs, running large multinational corporations, inflation is a real challenge.
turns.zh: 我觉得总体上还是乐观的。相比六个月、十二个月之前的状态，可能在边际上稍微谨慎了一点。通胀更高了，而这会传导到很多行业。所以尤其是对于那些执掌大型跨国公司的 CEO 来说，通胀是个实实在在的挑战。

turns.en: I think geopolitics continues to be a challenge. It hasn't necessarily gotten any better, maybe a little bit worse, particularly thinking about the Iran situation. And so I think more caution around the impact of the geopolitics on inflation and then obviously on rates.
turns.zh: 我认为地缘政治（geopolitics）依然是个挑战。情况并没有变好，甚至可能更糟了一点，尤其是想到伊朗那边的局势。所以我觉得大家会更谨慎地看待地缘政治对通胀、进而对利率的影响。

turns.en: So the environment we're in today, versus where it would have been six, twelve months ago, is we have higher inflation and we have higher rates. And so the cost of capital in the economy is higher. The cost of doing business from an inflation standpoint is higher. Fortunately, nominal growth is very good.
turns.zh: 所以今天我们所处的环境，跟六个月、十二个月前相比，是通胀更高、利率也更高。因此整个经济的资本成本更高了，从通胀角度看经营成本也更高了。好在名义增长（nominal growth）非常不错。

turns.en: So most companies are seeing pretty strong end demand and we still have very strong earnings. So I'm still on the side of optimism when I think about our clients and what they're feeling. A little bit more caution and a little bit more concern in the 27 planning.
turns.zh: 所以大多数公司看到的终端需求都相当强劲，盈利也依然很扎实。因此在想到我们的客户、想到他们的感受时，我还是站在乐观这一边。只不过在做 2027 年规划的时候，会多几分谨慎、多几分担忧。

turns.en: I think more of a concern about the impact, the continuous impact of higher prices, whether it's in inflation terms or in cost of capital terms. When you speak to CEOs and boards, what's really driving their decisions right now? Is it that more challenging, financing environment?
turns.zh: 我想更多的是对价格持续上涨所带来的影响的担忧——不管是通胀意义上的价格，还是资本成本意义上的价格。你跟这些 CEO 和董事会交流的时候，现在真正驱动他们决策的是什么？是那个更加棘手的融资环境吗？

turns.en: Obviously, you just discussed the geopolitical situation that may be a little bit worse. There's regulatory uncertainty as well. Is that beginning to weigh on their risk appetite or what are you observing in terms of their decision making? I think, first of all, we've had an extraordinary capital raising year.
turns.zh: 显然你刚才也提到地缘政治局势可能更糟了一些，此外还有监管上的不确定性。这些是不是开始压制他们的风险偏好（risk appetite）了？或者说，你在他们的决策过程中观察到了什么？——我觉得首先，我们刚刚度过了一个非同寻常的融资大年。

turns.en: So that tells you that companies are obviously AI is in the frame and everybody thinks it's all AI. So there's a lot of capital raising going on in the economy. People are building and growing and stands to reason. The U.S. economy is going to have nominal growth of north to 6%.
turns.zh: 这就说明企业端显然是活跃的——当然，AI 就在画面正中央，所有人都觉得一切都是 AI。所以整个经济里有大量融资在进行。大家在建设、在扩张，这也合乎情理：美国经济的名义增长会超过 6%。

turns.en: So there's plenty of good things going on and people are investing and spending accordingly. And the consumer is still very resilient. So I think whether it's the consumer end markets or the wholesale end markets, the enterprise end markets, markets are strong.
turns.zh: 所以有很多好事情在发生，大家也在相应地投资和支出。而且消费者依然非常有韧性。因此我认为不管是消费端市场，还是批发端、企业端市场，需求都很强劲。

turns.en: Obviously, it's not all the same all over the world, but I think particularly in the United States demand is very good. So companies see that they're investing into that. I do think there's a big bias for scale. So we see that in our M&A business where there's been a lot more corporate M&A of scale.
turns.zh: 当然，全球各地并不都一样，但我认为特别是在美国，需求非常好。所以企业看到了这一点，也在往里面投资。我确实认为存在一种很强的『规模偏好』（bias for scale）。这在我们的并购（M&A）业务里就能看到——大型的产业并购明显多了起来。

turns.en: The bias is the larger companies are attracting more capital. They're generating better returns on that capital. They're being treated better in the marketplace. There's more of an ability to spend into the AI theme and the thesis and actually get the value for the compute that is obviously very expensive.
turns.zh: 这种偏好体现在：更大的公司能吸引更多资本，能在这些资本上创造更好的回报，在市场里也受到更好的对待。它们更有能力在 AI 这个主题和逻辑上投入，真正从显然极其昂贵的算力（compute）中拿到价值。

turns.en: And so I think that theme continues to play forward and I think we will see more M&A on the forward from a corporate standpoint, which is generally speaking a pretty good indicator of CEO confidence. CEOs are not going to do M&A transactions if they're not feeling confident in their own business. Let me ask a couple of faults to that.
turns.zh: 所以我认为这个主题还会继续演绎下去，而且往后我们会看到更多企业端的并购。这通常是 CEO 信心的一个相当好的风向标——如果 CEO 对自己的业务没有信心，他们是不会去做并购交易的。——那让我就这一点追问几个问题。

turns.en: As you said, the economic resilience, it's actually been pretty striking. But the market has become more volatile. It may be pricing a little bit more uncertainty. How is the firm viewing the economic outlook ahead? We're constructive. As I said, nominal growth in the U.S. looks like it's going to be north to 6%.
turns.zh: 就像你说的，经济的韧性其实相当惊人。但市场波动性变大了，可能正在为更多的不确定性定价。公司如何看待接下来的经济前景？——我们是建设性乐观的（constructive）。正如我说的，美国的名义增长看起来会超过 6%。

turns.en: We obviously are running with hotter inflation. So real growth is in the twos, let's say. And I think you would know as well as I do, I think our forecast is 2.5% real growth plus minus. That's pretty strong. It could get to 3%. If things break in a certain way, we obviously think as a firm inflation will start to migrate down.
turns.zh: 我们显然面临着更热的通胀，所以实际增长（real growth）大概在 2% 出头的区间。我想你跟我一样清楚，我们的预测大约是 2.5% 左右的实际增长，上下浮动。这已经相当强了，如果事情往某个方向发展，甚至可能到 3%。作为一家公司，我们显然认为通胀会开始回落。

turns.en: And that could be quite helpful. So I'd say we're generally pretty constructive on the U.S. economy. I've been spending a lot of time in Asia. The Asia economies are very strong. China obviously is, it's almost a tale of two cities. It's kind of weak domestic economy, but very strong innovation economy and a lot of export growth.
turns.zh: 而那会带来相当大的帮助。所以我会说，我们对美国经济总体上是相当有信心的。我最近花了很多时间在亚洲。亚洲各经济体非常强劲。中国显然有点『双城记』（a tale of two cities）的味道——内需经济偏弱，但创新经济非常强，出口增长也很多。

turns.en: But generally speaking, growth in the U.S. and Asia very strong. Growth in Europe more muted. A little better than I think the narrative suggests. People are very down on Europe. It's actually a little bit better than would be the narrative. But I'd say generally speaking Europe is underperforming from a growth standpoint.
turns.zh: 但总体而言，美国和亚洲的增长非常强劲，欧洲的增长则更为温和。我觉得比市场叙事所暗示的要好一点——大家对欧洲非常悲观，实际情况比那个叙事要好一些。但我还是认为，从增长角度看，欧洲是落后的。

turns.en: But generally speaking, the environment's pretty constructive. Do you sense a difference in sentiment in Asia versus Europe relative to the U.S.? For sure, the sentiment in Europe is not good. I think the combination of politics, geopolitics, lack of energy security,
turns.zh: 不过整体来说，环境还是相当有建设性的。——你能感觉到亚洲、欧洲相对于美国，在情绪上的差别吗？——绝对有。欧洲的情绪不好。我认为政治、地缘政治、能源安全缺失这几件事叠加在一起，

turns.en: the war in Ukraine, the war in Iran, probably having a disproportionate impact on the European economies. I think the China export machine has been pretty pernicious for the European economy, particularly in places like Autos, where they're really feeling that excess supply coming into their marketplace at lower prices.
turns.zh: 加上乌克兰战争、伊朗战争，很可能对欧洲经济体造成了不成比例的冲击。我觉得中国的出口机器对欧洲经济来说一直是相当有害的（pernicious），尤其是在汽车这类领域——他们真切地感受到过剩供给以更低的价格涌入自己的市场。

turns.en: And so I think the sentiment in Europe is generally speaking not very good. I always feel like I have to give people a hug when I'm visiting European clients. I don't think it's as bad as they feel it, but they certainly feel it in a negative way. When you get to Asia, there's more buoyancy and more optimism.
turns.zh: 所以我认为欧洲的情绪总体上来讲不太好。我去拜访欧洲客户的时候，总觉得自己得给他们一个拥抱。我不觉得情况真像他们感觉的那么糟，但他们确实是以一种负面的方式在感受它。而到了亚洲，就有更多的活力和乐观。

turns.en: I'll take a market like Japan right was a few weeks ago. Japan has had a long run of relatively muted growth, but all of a sudden Japan's having a real moment. Where there is more growth, there is more loan demand. There's a little bit of a yield curve to work with now.
turns.zh: 拿日本这样的市场来说，我几周前刚去过。日本已经经历了很长一段时间的相对低迷的增长，但突然间，日本迎来了一个真正的高光时刻。增长多了，贷款需求就多了。现在也终于有了一条略微向上的收益率曲线（yield curve）可以经营。

turns.en: There's more of an asset management push to unlock a bunch of those lazy deposits. So Japan, all of a sudden, has much more positive sentiment. And so there are plenty of places in the world where the sentiment is quite strong. Europe, I would say, has the worst sentiment among those markets. In a lot of political turbulence as well.
turns.zh: 资产管理（asset management）方面的推力也更大了，要去激活一大堆『躺着不动』的存款。所以日本的情绪突然间正面了很多。也就是说，世界上有很多地方的情绪是相当强的。而欧洲，我会说，是这些市场里情绪最差的，政治上也动荡得多。

turns.en: You already started talking about actual activity versus sentiment. We think about where we are in the M&A cycle. There had been some starts and stops. It feels like there's more positive momentum now. Do you see that continuing? I do. We're going to see corporate M&A up 35% this year.
turns.zh: 你已经开始谈实际活动与情绪之间的差别了。如果我们想想自己处在并购周期的哪个位置——之前一直走走停停，现在感觉正向的动能更足了。你觉得这会持续下去吗？——会的。今年企业并购规模会上涨 35%。

turns.en: So that's a pretty healthy growth factor on what was already a pretty strong base. Should be a record year in M&A this year. And we look at our backlogs and our pipelines are very strong. With all that volume still coming through the marketplace, we still see a lot of appetite on the forward. And so you can feel pretty positive momentum.
turns.zh: 在一个本来就已经相当高的基数上，这是相当健康的增长速度。今年应该是并购的创纪录之年。我们看自己的在手项目（backlog）和项目储备（pipeline），都非常强劲。市场上还有那么多交易量在推进，往后我们依然看到很大的意愿。所以你能感受到相当正面的动能。

turns.en: And it's back to what I said earlier. I think the bias for scale is real. And these transactions, it's an interesting marketplace to me. Because typically in M&A you'll have a theme scale or maybe demurging and no scale or lack of scale or less scale.
turns.zh: 这就回到我前面说的：我认为『规模偏好』是真实存在的。这些交易——这个市场对我来说很有意思。因为通常在并购里，你要么有『规模』这个主题，要么就是『分拆合并』（demerger）——也就是没有规模、缺乏规模或者规模更小。

turns.en: We actually have scale arguments going on at the same time as we have fit and focus arguments going on. So we see a lot of spins, a lot of carve outs. So companies are getting bigger and stronger in the places where they see growth and where they think they can win. And they're getting out of the businesses.
turns.zh: 而我们现在是『规模』的论据和『契合与聚焦』（fit and focus）的论据同时在发生。所以我们看到很多分拆（spin）、很多业务剥离（carve-out）。企业在自己看到增长、认为自己能赢的地方变得更大更强，同时从另一些业务里退出。

turns.en: We're getting smaller in the businesses where they don't see those dynamics in play. And selling them the private equity firms or spinning them out to the public markets and finding ways to get out of those businesses. And so that is driving an offensive and defensive part of the M&A cycle. And I think that continues.
turns.zh: 在那些看不到上述驱动力的业务里，他们在变小，把这些业务卖给私募股权（private equity）机构，或者分拆到公开市场，想办法退出。这就同时驱动了并购周期中进攻性和防御性的两个部分，我认为这还会继续。

turns.en: I think the marketplace rewards companies that are large and growing and predominantly positioned in their areas of focus. And companies are being rewarded for getting out of businesses where those factors are in place. And the market is really rewarding that type of activity.
turns.zh: 我认为市场会奖励那些规模大、在增长、并且在聚焦领域占据主导地位的公司。企业因为退出那些不具备这些条件的业务而获得奖励。市场真的在奖励这类动作。

turns.en: With all of that in mind, John, where does the firm stand on its key priorities? Where do you see the most compelling growth opportunities over the next several years? I think financing is still an enormous opportunity in the world. There's an enormous need for capital. Obviously the AI build is front and center.
turns.zh: 带着这些背景，John，公司在关键优先事项上处在什么位置？未来几年你看到最有吸引力的增长机会在哪里？——我认为融资（financing）在世界上仍然是一个巨大的机会。资本的需求极其庞大，AI 的建设显然就在正中央。

turns.en: There's a lot of infrastructure that needs to get built in the world. There's still decarbonization opportunities in the world. So there's a lot of capital that's going to need to be sourced to finance this activity. And frankly, I look at governments as becoming a little less relevant at the margin because they're pretty levered.
turns.zh: 世界上还有大量基础设施需要建设，脱碳（decarbonization）的机会也依然存在。所以要为这些活动筹集的资本会非常多。坦白说，我认为政府在边际上会变得没那么重要，因为他们的杠杆已经很高了。

turns.en: We came out of COVID and the governments were the engine of fiscal stimulus to bring us back from the COVID challenges. And so the governments have levered up. And now the private sector, I think, is going to have to be a bigger engine of that capital formation.
turns.zh: 我们走出新冠的时候，政府是财政刺激（fiscal stimulus）的引擎，把我们从新冠的冲击中拉了回来。所以政府已经加满了杠杆。现在，我认为私营部门必须成为资本形成（capital formation）更大的引擎。

turns.en: So we're pretty optimistic about the opportunity to raise a lot of capital in the coming years. And Goldman Sach sits at the center of a lot of that capital formation. So I'm very bullish on that opportunity set. I'm quite bullish on Asia. I think there's going to be a lot of economic growth.
turns.zh: 所以我们对未来几年募集大量资本的机会相当乐观。而 Goldman Sachs 正处在这场资本形成的中心。所以我对这个机会集非常看好（bullish）。我也相当看好亚洲，我认为那里会有大量的经济增长。

turns.en: I think there's going to be a lot more opportunity. And again, we've got a very nice business there. And we've put a lot of investment on the ground in the important markets in Asia. And so I see a lot of opportunity across the marketplace in Asia.
turns.zh: 我认为机会会多得多。而且再说一次，我们在那边有一块很好的业务，也在亚洲那些重要市场投入了大量本地资源。所以我在整个亚洲市场看到了很多机会。

turns.en: And then I'd get back to asset and wealth management as big opportunities, certainly for Goldman Sachs. But I think from many firms, there's obviously an enormous amount of wealth creation that has occurred over the last five, ten years. And I think we'll continue to occur. And that wealth creation needs to be asset managed.
turns.zh: 然后我会回到资产管理（asset management）和财富管理（wealth management），这是很大的机会，对 Goldman Sachs 当然如此，但我认为对很多机构都是。过去五年、十年里显然发生了巨量的财富创造，我认为这还会继续。而这些创造出来的财富需要被管理起来。

turns.en: People need access to good products and solutions to manage their wealth accordingly. And firms like Goldman Sachs are exceptionally well positioned to do that. We've already talked about AI a few times in this conversation. It's really impossible not to talk about it, given the pervasiveness of the technology.
turns.zh: 人们需要获得好的产品和解决方案，来相应地管理自己的财富。而像 Goldman Sachs 这样的机构，在这件事上的定位极为有利。

turns.en: We're incorporating it in our core strategy at Goldman Sachs. Talk to us a little bit about how we're using the technology, the impact it's making. Yeah, AI is having a huge impact on our firm. And I'm very encouraged about the progress we've made at Goldman Sachs.
turns.zh: 我们在这次对话里已经几次提到 AI 了。考虑到这项技术的无处不在，实在不可能不谈它。我们正在把 AI 纳入 Goldman Sachs 的核心战略。跟我们讲讲我们在怎么用这项技术，它带来了什么样的影响。——是的，AI 对我们公司正在产生巨大的影响。我对 Goldman Sachs 已经取得的进展感到非常振奋。

turns.en: We basically have a four-pronged strategy, the first of which is literacy and adoption. So we want to get our employees as literate as possible and as comfortable using the tools as possible. So we've really done a lot of work putting tools out for our employees to use
turns.zh: 我们基本上有一个『四条腿』的战略（four-pronged strategy），第一条是素养与采用（literacy and adoption）。我们希望让员工尽可能具备 AI 素养、尽可能自在地使用这些工具。所以我们确实做了大量工作，把工具放到员工手上去用，

turns.en: and then teaching them how to think about using them and putting a lot of training out. And I think we've done well in that first pillar. The second is really around software development and software development life cycle, which is probably where I've seen the early wins in terms of efficiency and productivity.
turns.zh: 然后教他们怎么去思考这些工具的用法，并推出大量培训。我认为在第一个支柱上我们做得不错。第二个支柱真正围绕软件开发和软件开发生命周期（software development life cycle），这大概也是我在效率和生产力上看到最早期成果的地方。

turns.en: If you talk to the coders at Goldman Sachs, they would wax on about how valuable tools like it have been to Goldman Sachs in terms of driving a lot of coding, efficiency and productivity across the whole life cycle. And we think that will continue to accelerate.
turns.zh: 如果你去跟 Goldman Sachs 的程序员聊，他们会滔滔不绝地讲这类工具对公司有多有价值——在整个开发生命周期里带来了大量的编码效率和生产力。我们认为这还会继续加速。

turns.en: And that has a huge impact on Goldman Sachs because we write a lot of code in this firm, either because we're trying to deal with deferred maintenance on older systems or because we're trying to build new systems, new capabilities, new tools for our clients.
turns.zh: 这对 Goldman Sachs 影响巨大，因为在这家公司我们写非常多的代码——要么是在处理老系统积压的维护（deferred maintenance），要么是在搭建新系统、新能力、给客户的新工具。

turns.en: The third area is what I would put in the broad bucket of re-engineering the firm, which is automation. So we're not a manufacturing organization. We're a human capital organization, we're a services company. If we were a manufacturing company, we'd be talking about getting some robots on the floor.
turns.zh: 第三个领域，我会归到『重塑公司』（re-engineering the firm）这个大筐里，也就是自动化（automation）。我们不是制造业组织，我们是人力资本（human capital）组织，是服务公司。如果我们是一家制造企业，我们谈的就会是往车间里放一些机器人。

turns.en: We're using a lot of digital agents to start automating a lot of the processes that run across our organization that are, I call them the interstate highways, so they run across state lines. And they need to be automated because they've really not been automated in any real way over time. They're much more human-centric processes.
turns.zh: 我们正在用大量数字代理（digital agents）来自动化那些贯穿整个组织的流程——我把它们叫作『州际高速公路』，因为它们跨越州界（跨部门）。这些流程需要被自动化，因为长期以来它们其实根本没有被真正自动化过，更多是以人为中心的流程。

turns.en: So there's a big opportunity for us to unlock and make the firm more resilient, more scalable, not really just about taking cost up, but frankly about building a stronger foundation for which we can grow. And then the fourth area is really around tools for clients. Can we use the Goldman Sachs data, which is extensive,
turns.zh: 所以对我们来说，这里有一个很大的机会去释放价值、让公司更有韧性、更可扩展，其实并不只是为了砍成本，坦白说更是为了打造一个更强的地基，让我们能在上面增长。然后第四个领域真正围绕给客户的工具。我们能不能把 Goldman Sachs 那些极为丰富的数据——

turns.en: and now in a much cleaner shape than it would have been 5-10 years ago? Plus our human capital, our judgment, our experience, plus the technology of LLMs and digital agents. And can we package all that together and can we give our clients better advice faster? And that I'm very excited about.
turns.zh: 而且现在的数据形态比五到十年前干净得多——再加上我们的人力资本、我们的判断力和经验，再加大语言模型（LLM）和数字代理这些技术，我们能不能把这一切打包起来，更快、更好地给客户提供建议？这一点我非常兴奋。

turns.en: I think we're just on the beginning stages of coming up with some tools that we can bring to our clients in an environment that is the Goldman Sachs environment, coupled with our human intelligence. I think those two things married together can be quite powerful, and I think we're going to make a lot of progress.
turns.zh: 我认为我们才刚刚处在起步阶段，正在做出一些可以带给客户的工具，而且是在 Goldman Sachs 的环境里、与我们的人类智能（human intelligence）结合在一起。我认为这两者结合在一起会相当强大，我们会取得很多进展。

turns.en: So we're putting a lot more tools out there. We're building a lot more use cases. We're working with a lot of partners, LLMs and hyperscalers and other compute providers to make sure that we have the capacity to do what we want to do. And I'm very encouraged about the progress.
turns.zh: 所以我们在推出更多工具，构建更多用例（use case），也在跟很多伙伴合作——LLM 公司、超大规模云厂商（hyperscalers）以及其他算力供应商——以确保我们有能力去做我们想做的事。我对这些进展感到非常鼓舞。

turns.en: And I think 2027 is going to be a much bigger year for Goldman Sachs and our deployment of AI than 2026 was, which was also quite a good start for us. So a lot going on and a lot to look forward to on the AI front. Let me just get back to the growth front for a moment. The firm has recently made a series of targeted acquisitions,
turns.zh: 我认为对 Goldman Sachs 和我们的 AI 部署来说，2027 年会是比 2026 年大得多的一年，而 2026 年对我们来说也已经是个相当不错的开端。所以 AI 这条线上事情很多，值得期待的东西也很多。——让我先回到增长这条线上。公司最近做了一系列有针对性的收购，

turns.en: industry ventures, innovator, neosinvestments, and LCN capital partners. What's strategic thinking behind these specialized acquisitions? Why now? And how do you approach integrating several unique platforms simultaneously? So we have one of the top five asset managers in the world. We are very scaled.
turns.zh: Industry Ventures、Innovator、NEOS Investments，还有 LCN Capital Partners。这些专业化收购背后的战略思考是什么？为什么是现在？以及你要如何同时整合几个各自独特的平台？——我们拥有全球前五的资产管理机构之一，我们的规模很大。

turns.en: We're north to $4 trillion of assets on our platform. And we've long believed that global broad and deep is an important thought process around running a scaled asset manager. So we want to have the capabilities in all the important NASA classes.
turns.zh: 我们平台上的资产超过 4 万亿美元（$4 trillion）。我们长期以来一直相信，『全球化、广而深』（global, broad and deep）是运营一家规模化资产管理机构的重要思路。所以我们希望在所有重要的资产类别（asset classes）里都具备能力。

turns.en: We want to be very deep with our expertise and we want to obviously be very global in our approach. When you think about it that way, there are places where we are either not big enough or we don't really have the capabilities that we want to have. And we could of course go about setting our course on building those capabilities.
turns.zh: 我们希望自己的专业积累非常深，也希望在打法上显然非常全球化。当你这样去想的时候，就会发现有些地方我们要么规模不够大，要么并不真正具备我们想要的能力。我们当然可以自己定下路线去建设这些能力。

turns.en: But there are acquisitions you can make to make that go faster and to really fill in those gaps in an important way. So the gaps would be either around solutions, asset classes, where we want to be stronger and better, or distribution. So I'll give you a good example. We actually did a partnership with T.R. Price.
turns.zh: 但有些收购能让你走得更快，真正以重要的方式补上那些缺口。所以这些缺口要么在解决方案（solutions）上，要么在我们希望做得更强、更好的资产类别上，要么在分销（distribution）上。我给你举个好例子：我们其实跟 T. Rowe Price 做了一个合作。

turns.en: It wasn't an acquisition. We just formed essentially a partnership together with them. T.R. Price has one of the largest and best retirement platforms in the United States. Goldman Sachs doesn't have that. We're not very likely to build a retirement platform from scratch anytime soon.
turns.zh: 那不是收购，我们基本上只是和他们组成了一个合作关系。T. Rowe Price 拥有美国最大、最好的退休（retirement）平台之一。Goldman Sachs 没有这样的平台，而且我们短期内也不太可能从零开始自建一个退休平台。

turns.en: But we can partner with T.R. Price and have access to their retirement platform and we can marry their expertise in our expertise in public markets and in private markets to design products and solutions that fit the retirement savers in America. And so we're going about doing that, whether it's model portfolios, private credit,
turns.zh: 但我们可以跟 T. Rowe Price 合作，用上他们的退休平台，把他们在这一领域的专长与我们在公开市场和私募市场上的专长结合起来，设计出适合美国退休储蓄者的产品和解决方案。所以我们正在这么做——不管是模型组合（model portfolios）、私募信贷（private credit）、

turns.en: interval fund structures, multi-asset public-private structures. We're starting to really work on some pretty interesting solutions that serve their retirement customers and clients and also serve the broader wealth channel. Industry Ventures is a venture capital platform embedded in the Silicon Valley ecosystem.
turns.zh: 区间基金（interval fund）结构，还是公私混合的多资产结构。我们开始真正在做一些相当有意思的解决方案，既服务他们的退休客户，也服务更广泛的财富渠道。Industry Ventures 是一个嵌在硅谷（Silicon Valley）生态里的风险投资（venture capital）平台。

turns.en: Very synergistic for Goldman Sachs. Phenomenal track record of raising capital and deploying capital and venture capital transactions up and down the ecosystem. We've done transactions in leasing net lease platform, which is LCN, innovator and NEOS or ETF platform. So in each area, we're building strength and capabilities
turns.zh: 对 Goldman Sachs 来说协同性非常强。它在募资和投放资本方面有极为出色的过往业绩，风险投资交易覆盖整个生态的上下游。我们还做了租赁方面的交易——净租赁（net lease）平台，也就是 LCN；还有 Innovator，以及 NEOS，那是 ETF 平台。所以在每一个领域，我们都在建设实力和能力，

turns.en: where we otherwise were small and not as strong as we want to be or we don't have the distribution heft that we would like to have. And so we're finding places to fill in those gaps. And then your integration question is a really important question. So we have not done that many acquisitions in our history at Goldman Sachs.
turns.zh: 补上那些我们原本规模偏小、没有做到我们想要那么强的地方，或者我们原本不具备希望拥有的分销分量的地方。所以我们在找机会填补这些缺口。然后你那个关于整合的问题，是个非常重要的问题。在 Goldman Sachs 的历史上，我们做的收购其实并不多。

turns.en: This firm has been relatively organically built. We are now building the capability to integrate acquisitions and find ways to build playbooks and be more systematic about how we acquire something and make it fit into our company. And I think we're getting better at it. Every transaction we do, we get a little bit sharper.
turns.zh: 这家公司基本上是靠内生方式（organically）建起来的。我们现在正在建设整合收购的能力，想办法建立操作手册（playbook），让『怎么收购一家公司、怎么把它融进我们体系』这件事更系统化。我认为我们在变好。每做一笔交易，我们就更敏锐一点。

turns.en: And we're trying to build something that we can repeat. So yes, each transaction has its own elements. The most important thing is culture. We have to make sure that when we buy companies or assets and people that we think the cultural fit will be strong. And we can actually bring those people into our firm
turns.zh: 我们在努力打造一套可以复制的东西。所以是的，每笔交易都有它自己的特点。但最重要的是文化（culture）。我们必须确保，当我们收购公司、资产和团队的时候，文化契合度是强的，我们真的能把这些人纳入公司，

turns.en: and they can feel like they're part of Goldman Sachs and they've always been part of Goldman Sachs. And so we spent a lot of time on the early part of the diligence process thinking about that. And then we get to the integration part. We work hard to make sure those cultural integrations are strong.
turns.zh: 让他们觉得自己是 Goldman Sachs 的一部分，而且好像一直就是其中一员。所以在尽调（diligence）的早期阶段，我们会花很多时间去想这件事。然后到了整合环节，我们也会努力确保文化层面的整合是扎实的。

turns.en: And I think so far we've done a very good job in these recent acquisitions and I'm encouraged about our opportunity to do more of those. Let's expand on that culture point. It is so important. We often say that culture is the defining asset of Goldman Sachs. Our people are our defining asset.
turns.zh: 我认为到目前为止，在这几笔近期收购上我们做得非常好，这也让我对将来做更多这类交易的机会感到鼓舞。——那我们就把『文化』这一点展开讲讲，它太重要了。我们常说，文化是 Goldman Sachs 的定义性资产，我们的人才是我们的定义性资产。

turns.en: How do you preserve what's distinctive about the firm's culture as we grow, as we diversify, and bring in a new generation of talent, some of which may be AI agents? Yeah, listen, culture is the most important thing at Goldman Sachs. We're a human capital organization. We're going to be human capital organization.
turns.zh: 在公司成长、多元化、并引入新一代人才——其中一些可能还是 AI 代理——的过程中，你要如何保住这家公司文化里那些独特的东西？——是的，听着，文化在 Goldman Sachs 是最重要的事情。我们是人力资本组织，我们将来也还是会继续是人力资本组织。

turns.en: Yes, we're going to deploy digital agents, but we're still going to be human capital organization. We rely on that talent to really propel the firm forward and talent on its own not working collaboratively together is not going to get it done.
turns.zh: 是的，我们会部署数字代理，但我们仍然会是一家人力资本组织。我们依靠人才去真正推动公司向前，而人才如果各自为战、不协同工作，是成不了事的。

turns.en: We have to bring that talent together and have that talent really want to work as a cohesive unit. That's really all about one Goldman Sachs. One Goldman Sachs has been successful because we've been able to take the talent that we have and get it to work together to be even more powerful than any individual talent would have been.
turns.zh: 我们必须把这些人才聚到一起，让他们真正愿意作为一个有凝聚力的整体去工作。这其实讲的就是『一个 Goldman Sachs』（One Goldman Sachs）。『一个 Goldman Sachs』之所以成功，是因为我们能把拥有的人才组织起来协同工作，从而比任何单个人才都要更强大。

turns.en: And so I think for us, to me, culture is about narrating the words, what does it mean? When we say collaborative, what does it mean? Let's bring it to life. So I think both in terms of the actual narration, the examples of the words that you want to use showing people what it means, celebrating those victories when you see it in action,
turns.zh: 所以我认为，对我们来说，文化在于把这些词讲清楚：它到底意味着什么？当我们说『协作』（collaborative）的时候，它意味着什么？让我们把它变得鲜活。所以我认为，一方面是真正的讲述——你想用的那些词的示例，向大家展示它意味着什么，在你看到它真正发生时去庆祝这些胜利；

turns.en: helping people understand when you see things that are not core to the culture happening in the firm, how we get rid of that, how we stop that, how we change that. I think teaching people how to embrace AI and use AI and make it a core part of what makes the firm special and unique
turns.zh: 另一方面，是帮助大家理解：当你看到公司里发生了并不属于我们文化核心的事情时，我们怎么去消除它、怎么去制止它、怎么去改变它。我认为，教会大家如何拥抱 AI、使用 AI，让它成为这家公司之所以特别、之所以独特的核心的一部分，

turns.en: and how it can be in the service of clients is going to be really important for us. So yes, having digital agents will be part of the firm. They've got to be in the name and service of clients, or in the name of service of making the firm or resilient and scalable so we can serve our clients better.
turns.zh: 以及它如何能够服务于客户，这对我们会非常重要。所以是的，数字代理会成为公司的一部分。但它们必须是以客户之名、为客户服务，或者是为了让公司更有韧性、更可扩展，从而让我们能更好地服务客户。

turns.en: And I think that'll be the way we narrate and work hard at that aspect of the culture. That's a good note to end on. But I do have a final question, which is what advice would you give to someone starting their career in finance today and how does that advice change? Given that the nature of work itself is changing.
turns.zh: 我认为这就是我们去讲述、并在这个文化面向上努力下功夫的方式。——这是个不错的收尾点。但我确实还有最后一个问题：对于今天刚开始金融职业生涯的人，你会给出什么建议？而当工作本身的性质正在改变时，这个建议又会有什么不同？

turns.en: Yeah, I think intellectual curiosity to me is pretty important. It's always been important right now, it may be even more important. Now the good news with all these tools that we have in LLM modeling capability is you can learn a lot quickly. And I think when you come into a firm like ours
turns.zh: 是的，我认为求知欲（intellectual curiosity）对我来说相当重要。它一直都重要，而现在可能更重要了。好消息是，有了这些工具和大语言模型（LLM）的建模能力，你可以很快学到很多东西。我认为当你进入像我们这样的公司时，

turns.en: being intellectually curious and being willing to learn is going to serve you very well. We can give you a lot of information. The technology can amplify that. And your willingness to absorb all that and be willing to take some risks and learn things that you don't otherwise really know well.
turns.zh: 保持求知欲、愿意学习，会让你受益良多。我们能给你大量信息，技术还能把这些信息放大。而你要愿意吸收这一切，愿意承担一些风险，去学习那些你本来并不真正熟悉的东西。

turns.en: Work on your weaknesses, get a little smarter in areas where you haven't had that same kind of background in your development. I think all those areas are really important. So that's what I say to young people coming into the firm is be very open-minded, be a sponge, and just learn. Because we're going to show you and offer you
turns.zh: 去补自己的短板，在那些你在成长过程中没有同样背景积累的领域变得更聪明一点。我认为这些方面都非常重要。所以这就是我对刚进公司的年轻人说的：要非常开放，要像海绵一样，就是去学。因为我们会向你展示、向你提供

turns.en: an enormous amount of information and perspective and experience and judgment that you can learn over time. And that's going to be the most important thing. I mean, it's never been a better moment, I think, for young people to embrace that experience and learn. I agree. I think there's a lot of concern on college campuses.
turns.zh: 海量的信息、视角、经验和判断力，让你随时间去学习。这才是最重要的事情。我的意思是，对年轻人来说，从来没有比现在更好的时刻去拥抱这种经验、去学习。——我同意。我认为大学校园里有很多担忧。

turns.en: I see it in the eyes of young students when I go to those campuses that they're worried about, can they get a job? Is this world going to be hospitable for them? I'm much more optimistic. I think particularly if you're willing to learn and you show that desire to stretch your mind, this is an extraordinary time.
turns.zh: 我去那些校园的时候，能从年轻学生的眼神里看到，他们在担心：自己能不能找到工作？这个世界对他们来说还会是友好的吗？我要乐观得多。我认为，尤其是如果你愿意学习、并且展现出那种想要拓展自己心智的渴望，这是一个非凡的时代。

turns.en: We need a lot of talent at Goldman Sachs. We need on-board young talent, young energy. They're going to be very facile with the tools. I think it's going to be an extraordinary period for young talent in our firm and in the economy more broadly. Thank you so much for sharing your insights, John. Always a pleasure.
turns.zh: 我们在 Goldman Sachs 需要大量人才。我们需要引入年轻的人才、年轻的能量。他们会对这些工具非常熟练。我认为对我们公司、以及对更广泛的经济来说，这都会是年轻人才的一段非凡时期。——非常感谢你分享你的洞见，John。——一直都很愉快。

turns.en: Nice to be here. Thank you. This episode of Goldman Sachs Extensions was equated on Tuesday, November 3rd, 2026. If you enjoyed the show, we'll help you subscribe to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, or wherever you get your podcasts, and leave us a rating and comment. I'm also Nathan. Thanks for listening.
turns.zh: 很高兴来到这里，谢谢。——本期 Goldman Sachs Exchanges 录制于 2026 年 11 月 3 日星期二。如果你喜欢这档节目，请帮忙订阅 Apple Podcasts、Spotify，或者你平时听播客的任何平台，并给我们留下评分和评论。我是 Allison Nathan，感谢收听。
